memory_bridge: Turn the two strokes into a February calendar shelf: 二月 supplies formal On ニ, while two objects placed on the two shelves are 二つ for Kun ふたつ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 二月（にがつ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Write 二月（にがつ） across the two-line February calendar; the opening sound fixes On ニ in “February.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 二つ（ふたつ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Set one orange on each stroke and count the pair 二つ（ふたつ）; the full native counter word fixes Kun ふたつ, “two.”

memory_bridge: Keep the thread-delayed walker behind a moving clock: 午後 marks the afternoon with On ゴ, 後 points to what comes later with Kun あと, and 後ろ points to the space at the back with Kun うしろ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 午後（ごご）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: The delayed walker finally arrives when the clock reads 午後（ごご）, “afternoon”; the second character repeats the On sound ゴ.

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 後（あと）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Leave a note on the path saying “come later” and label that later point 後（あと）; the standalone native word fixes Kun あと, “after; later.”

readings.editorial_reason: Promoted because 後ろ（うしろ）is common, modern, and pedagogically useful.
readings.overlay: Look back and find the thread-tangled foot still 後ろ（うしろ）, at the back; the complete native location word fixes Kun うしろ.
